I can say that it doesn’t make a winning argument: The two characterizations nullify each other, leaving the audience to shrug.
It’s a juicy setup steeped in satire, and the playwright doubles down by flipping the script on gender.
Mattana offers an eye-opening look at the rising ruling class of this country on the eve of its 249th birthday in Trophy Boys, now making its US premiere at MCC Theater.

Trophy Boys certainly excels in exposing the performative contradictions of male allyship, particularly through the teenage debaters' cynical, absurd improvisations, rife with logical fallacies and desperate deflections and rationalizations.
It also ends on an appropriately bruising note as the young men gin up an array of legalistic arguments that, alas, may very well protect them from the consequences of their actions.
Mattana has set up a wonderful premise, but then doesn’t quite know where to take it.
Taymor’s production is a humorous, stiff-upper-lipped response to repressive times.

cn.t: Mattana's sharp satire about elite prep school debaters earns praise for its inventive gender-swapped casting and provocative ideas, though critics are mixed on execution. The snappy 70-minute comedy delivers barbed humor but doesn't fully land for all.
